findings.title: Local cache is populated before the DB write, so a rejected device bypasses the limit on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the key stays cached (TTL about 29 minutes). The device's next request hits the cache, returns nil from `tagDeviceUI`, and `Authenticate` succeeds. A device over the limit is therefore rejected only once, then allowed for the cache window without being recorded. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or removed on error.

findings.title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session, then performs the upsert in a separate one, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see `count < limit` and all insert, so the limit can be exceeded, especially under bursts when many new anonymous devices arrive at once. A conditional insert (INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE count < limit) or a transaction would enforce it.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from background goroutine into the request path
findings.body: The previous code tagged the device asynchronously with a detached 2-minute context and panic recovery. It now runs synchronously on the request context. Every uncached anonymous request pays for a COUNT query plus a write when the limit is enabled, and a cancelled request context aborts tagging. The panic recovery was also removed. This is needed to return the limit error, but it adds latency and DB load, and nothing in the PR acknowledges or mitigates it.

findings.title: Frontend type and default disagree with the backend payload
findings.body: The Go DTO always sends `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` (0 when unset). The frontend types it as `number | undefined`, and `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` infers the property type as `undefined` in the class. The typing is inconsistent, and the frontend cannot distinguish 'no limit' (0) from unset.

findings.title: New `device_limit` option is undocumented
findings.body: The new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` setting is read here but not added to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini` or the docs. The PR description is also an empty template. Operators have no way to discover the option or learn its semantics (0 = unlimited, 30-day window, rejection behaviour).

findings.title: Limit tests are thin
findings.body: The only new test checks that a second new device is rejected at limit 1. There is no test that an existing device can still update at the limit, that expired devices stop counting toward the limit, or that `Anonymous.Authenticate` returns the error. The cache-bypass bug on rejected devices would also be caught by a service-level test.
